answers.explanation: One shared bus connects them all to memory, which is why they compete for memory cycles.
The disk can be transferring data while the CPU runs a program. That overlap is what makes computers fast.
Data moves between the device and the local buffer, then between the buffer and main memory.
The controller fills its buffer from the device; the CPU copies between the buffer and main memory.
Interrupts are how hardware gets the CPU's attention.
The driver hides the details of one controller behind a standard interface.
A controller handles one TYPE of device, but may run several of them. A USB controller runs many USB devices.
A memory controller arbitrates between them on the common bus.
